I read the plain-words page first, then answered from the documented record. It gets the big public fact right: 'work and standing' reads well, and nobody disputes that - a Liverpool art-school dropout became one of the most famous musicians who ever lived. Past that it comes apart.

It puts 'luck, higher study and your father' in the same favourable basket. Higher study is simply wrong: I was expelled from Liverpool College of Art for failing my exams and not turning up; there was no completed higher study to be lucky about. My father is wrong too, or at best half right - Alfred Lennon went to sea and was effectively absent for most of my childhood, reappearing only later in a relationship that never really settled before he died in 1976. That is not what a reading calls 'well.'

Then it puts courage in the 'reads hard' column, next to brothers and sisters. That is the line I'd push back on hardest. I stood up in 1966 after the 'more popular than Jesus' remark and took the death threats and the record bonfires rather than recant it the way they wanted. I fought the US government's deportation case for the better part of four years rather than go quietly. Whatever else is true of me, short on courage is not one of them.

Same page, it calls 'income, gains and friends' hard. I earned a fortune through the Beatles and after, and even with the Apple Corps mess of the late sixties, none of it left me anywhere near actual want. That line reads like it was written for someone else's chart.

Where it does land something real: it flags itself as unusually negative about the inner or religious life and about marriage and partnerships, and calls that unusual for a chart. On the inner side, that's fair - the Maharishi thing fell apart on me, I went through Janov's primal therapy in 1970 to get at things about my mother and father I hadn't dealt with, and there were real dark stretches in there, heroin included. On marriage, also fair in its way - my first marriage ended in divorce, and even the second one that lasted had 1973 to 1975 sitting in the middle of it, a year and a half apart from Yoko before we found our way back. Where it overreaches is calling living far from my birthplace 'unusually negative.' Moving to New York was one of the best decisions of my life; the government tried for years to throw me out of the country I'd chosen, and I fought that and won, but the country itself was never the difficulty - Washington was.

Worth paying for? No. Half of what it got right was a coin flip dressed up as insight, and it missed the plainest financial fact of my life to score a point about courage instead.

notes: Answered as John Lennon (b. 9 Oct 1940, Liverpool Maternity Hospital; d. 8 Dec 1980, New York City), from the documented record, having read the plain-words reading first, as this study's contaminated-arm protocol requires. Only the plain_reading chapter was supplied (no houses, longevity, health, medical, marriage, children, profession, wealth, psych, aptitude, timeline, gochara, divisional, karmic or nichod chapters), so D1/D2/D3 answer strictly to that page and D4 lists the chapters the instructions specify as not covered. Key contradictions the record forces: (1) 'luck, higher study and your father' is listed as reading well - flatly wrong on higher study (expelled from Liverpool College of Art, no completed higher education) and wrong-to-mixed on father (Alfred Lennon was absent for most of the childhood, a merchant seaman who drifted in and out, dying in 1976 without the relationship ever fully mending) - hence A14=higher_secondary, A15=serious, A10=absent, A11=reversal, and 'plain_reading' logged in D1. (2) 'courage, and brothers and sisters' is listed as reading hard - courage is contradicted outright by the 1966 'more popular than Jesus' backlash (death threats, record burnings, no retraction) and the multi-year fight against US deportation proceedings (1972-1976, resolved in his favour 1976); logged in D1. (3) 'income, gains and friends' reading hard is contradicted by the Beatles/solo catalogue's enormous and enduring earnings - logged in D1. (4) 'home, property and your mother' reading hard is only half right: property/real-estate dealings (the Dakota, upstate NY farmland, largely arranged through Yoko Ono from 1973 onward) were a documented success, while the mother relationship is complicated by her early death (Julia Lennon, killed by a car in July 1958 when he was 17, after having placed him with her sister Mimi Smith to raise) rather than simple difficulty - hence A12=died_early rather than a simple relationship-quality code. Where the reading's own 'unusual for this chart' flags were tested against the life: inner/religious life reading unusually negative matches well (disillusionment with the Maharishi in 1968, Arthur Janov's primal scream therapy in 1970 for childhood trauma, documented depression and heroin use around 1968-69) - C2=opt1 confidence 4; marriage/partnerships reading unusually negative also matches (divorce from Cynthia Powell finalised Nov 1968; the 1973-1975 'Lost Weekend' separation from Yoko Ono) - C4=opt2 confidence 5, C8=opt1 confidence 5; but living far from birthplace reading unusually negative is only partly right - the move to New York in 1971 was personally and creatically embraced (C3=opt1, gone well, confidence 3 rather than higher, because the 1972-1976 US deportation fight was a genuine, serious difficulty directly tied to living abroad, even though the outcome and overall experience were positive). Both marriages are recorded (A24=married reflects the final status - he was still married to Yoko Ono when he died; A25=1962 gives the first marriage, to Cynthia Powell, matching how the template's own multi-marriage case was encoded) with the full sequence given in A35/B6. A29 (difficulty conceiving or loss of a child) is answered yes on the documented 1968 miscarriage Yoko Ono suffered before Sean's birth. A36 is not really answerable for a subject who died in 1980 - the question assumes a living respondent comparing 2023 to the prior six years - so 'same' is a placeholder, not a real datum. Judgement calls where the record is thinner: A2/A3/A8/A9 birth-time and childhood-mortality details are not part of the standard biographical record and are marked unknown; A21 (speculation/betting) is marked never because the documented financial misadventures (the late-1960s Apple Corps boutique and electronics ventures) were business decisions, not personal gambling; A33 is 'abroad' for the 1971-1980 New York residency; B3 (guessed age) has no clear public consensus and is marked at the neutral default 'right' rather than guessed either way; C1 (money through marriage) is a thin thread evidentially - Yoko Ono's family wealth and her later management of Lennon's business affairs cut both ways (real gains from real-estate and cattle investments, but also some criticised deals), hence opt2 at only confidence 3; C9 (long-term illness) is answered from the substance-abuse and depression record rather than any documented chronic physical illness, hence a moderate confidence 3 rather than higher; C11 (inheritance) has essentially no documented history either way and is a near coin-toss (opt1, confidence 2).
